english.title: Company / officer fail to give notice to person / entity if relevant change has occurred in PSC register
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), were

(A)_[a company which]_
(B)_[an officer, namely **(..SPECIFY OFFICER..) of a company, namely **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..) and who was in default in that the company]_

failed to comply with its duty to give notice to a registrable

(C)_[person]_
(D)_[relevant legal entity]_

whose particulars were stated in a company's PSC register, when it knew or had reasonable cause to believe that a relevant change, namely **(..SPECIFY CHANGE..), had occurred, as soon as reasonably practicable, and in any event before the end of the period of 14 days beginning with the earlier of the day after it learnt of the change and the day after it first had reasonable cause to believe that the change had occurred
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 790E(2) and 790F(2) of the Companies Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) This offence is no longer in force from 18/11/2025. Section 790E was substituted for new sections 790CB, 790D, 790DA, 790E, 790EA, 790EB and 790EC by the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 from 18/11/2025. This introduced a new statutory scheme for the company duties in relation to registerable people and legal entities. Failure to perform the duties contained within the legislation are offences under section 790F.
(ii) Civil financial penalties may be issued by the registrar for this offence being a ‘relevant offence’ as defined by section 1132A of the Companies Act 2006. No criminal proceedings may be commenced against a person in respect of conduct amounting to an offence if the person has already been given a financial penalty by the registrar. Further, no financial penalty may be imposed on a person in relation to conduct amounting to an offence if proceedings in respect of that offence are ongoing or the person has been convicted.
